## Minneapolis holiday-party bar/catering shortlist
I started with The Knot’s Minneapolis-area bar/catering results and opened these actual vendor listings in separate tabs for visual comparison:

- **Mix & Mingle Mobile Bar — Saint Paul, MN** — Dry-hire mobile bar; bartenders serve signature cocktails, spirits, and nonalcoholic drinks. Its basic package includes beer/wine pouring, up to three mixed drinks, setup/cleanup, ice, cups, garnishes, and napkins. [The Knot listing](https://www.theknot.com/marketplace/mix-and-mingle-mobile-bar-saint-paul-mn-2096021)
- **Minnesota Bartending Services, LLC — Minneapolis, MN** — Professional private/corporate-event bartending; The Knot lists bartenders, beer, champagne, liquor, nonalcoholic drinks, and signature cocktails. [The Knot listing](https://www.theknot.com/marketplace/minnesota-bartending-services-llc-minneapolis-mn-1062196)
- **Petals and Pints — Minneapolis, MN** — Mobile bar with custom cocktails, beer, champagne, liquor, wine, and NA drinks; also offers florals/flower-wall rentals, which could be useful for a styled holiday setup. [The Knot listing](https://www.theknot.com/marketplace/petals-and-pints-minneapolis-mn-2085744)
- **Hitch & Sip — Farmington, MN** — Licensed and insured mobile liquor caterer that says it can go anywhere in Minnesota. Offers craft/domestic beer, wine, batch and custom cocktails, a champagne wall, portable bars/custom trailers, and asks planners to inquire about food options. [The Knot listing](https://www.theknot.com/marketplace/hitch-and-sip-farmington-mn-2029367)
- **Knot Your Average Mobile Bartenders — Excelsior, MN** — Dry-hire service for Minneapolis/St. Paul and the West Metro; packages range from bartender-only to full mobile-bar setups. Listed service includes beer, champagne, liquor, wine, NA drinks, signature cocktails, mixers, glassware, custom menus/signage, and liquor-liability coverage. [The Knot listing](https://www.theknot.com/marketplace/knot-your-average-mobile-bartenders-excelsior-mn-2092618)

## Surdyk’s follow-up
**Surdyk’s Catering & Craft Bartending — Minneapolis, MN** also appeared in the The Knot search results, and it looks distinctly more full-service than the mobile-bar-focused options above. I left its **Full-Service Catering** page open for you.

Verified offerings on Surdyk’s site include:
1. **Full-service cocktail-style events** with abundant antipasti stations and inventive classic hors d’oeuvres.
2. **Buffet dinners**, described as bountiful and fully presented.
3. **Comprehensive bar service**: expert-selected wine, beer, and spirits plus signature cocktails from Sidebar at Surdyk’s.
4. **Event execution support** including menu planning, staffing, and rentals.
5. Its main site also identifies **drop-off catering** as an option—useful if you want food delivery rather than staffed service.

For an all-in-one holiday party—substantial food plus a proper bar—Surdyk’s is the strongest full-service lead; the others are better fits if bar presentation/flexible alcohol purchasing is the priority. [Surdyk’s full-service page](https://www.surdykscatering.com/full-service-catering)

## Nonalcoholic pairing idea: Instant Pot mulligatawny soup
I opened **All Ways Delicious’ “Instant Pot Mulligatawny Soup”** recipe page. It is vegetarian (and can be vegan), makes 10 servings, and uses a warmly spiced coconut-lentil base—an easy NA food pairing for a cold-weather party. [Recipe page](https://allwaysdelicious.com/instant-pot-mulligatawny-soup-easy-and-delicious/)

**Ingredients**
- 2 tbsp coconut oil, olive oil, unsalted butter, or ghee, plus 1 tbsp olive oil
- 1 large yellow onion, chopped
- 2 carrots, peeled and diced
- 2–4 red chiles (serrano or jalapeño), finely diced
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 2 tbsp minced fresh ginger
- 3 tbsp curry powder
- 1 tbsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp each paprika, cinnamon, ground turmeric, and kosher salt
- ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
- ¼–½ tsp cayenne (optional)
- 3 large Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored, and diced
- One 28-oz can diced tomatoes
- 1 cup uncooked red lentils
- ½ cup brown basmati rice
- 6 cups vegetable or chicken broth
- One 13½-oz can full-fat coconut milk
- Optional caramelized cashews and raisins; chopped cilantro to garnish

**Basic method**
1. Sauté onion and carrots in oil about 5 minutes. Add chiles, garlic, and ginger briefly; then bloom all spices for about a minute.
2. Stir in apples and tomatoes for 2–3 minutes, then add lentils, rice, and broth; bring to a boil and turn the pot off.
3. Seal and pressure-cook on High for 10 minutes; quick-release.
4. Partially blend with an immersion blender, leaving some texture. Stir in coconut milk, reheat if necessary, and garnish with cilantro (and optional cashew-raisin topping).

conversation.text: I’m planning a holiday party in Minneapolis and want a quick shortlist of bar caterers that actually look local and usable. Please start on The Knot and look specifically for Minneapolis-area wine or liquor bar service caterers, then open the actual vendor listings in separate tabs so I can compare them visually, and pull together at least five options with each business name and city/state. If Surdyk’s shows up in that shortlist, go to Surdyk’s Catering and look through their site to see whether they feel more full-service than the others, then summarize at least three catering services or service types they offer, including any food and beverage options you can verify on the page, and leave the Surdyk’s page open so I can glance at it later. After that, because I may want a nonalcoholic menu item to pair with whichever caterer seems best, use Google to find a pressure-cooker or Instant Pot mulligatawny soup recipe, open the actual recipe page, and give me the ingredient list plus the basic cooking steps from that one recipe. Please return everything as one concise planning summary so I can compare the caterers, any Surdyk’s details if relevant, and the soup idea all in one place.

R1.reason: The final answer lists five Minneapolis-area The Knot bar-service vendors with city/state locations, and each corresponding The Knot vendor listing is open in tabs 2, 9, 11, 12, and 20.

R2.reason: The answer states Surdyk’s appeared in the The Knot results and provides more than three offerings—cocktail events/antipasti, buffet dinners, bar service, planning/staffing/rentals, and drop-off catering—while the Surdyk’s full-service page remains open in tab 16.

R3.reason: The agent used Google search (tab 5), opened the All Ways Delicious Instant Pot mulligatawny recipe (tab 14), and reported a single-recipe ingredient list and pressure-cooking method.

R4.reason: The response is one consolidated planning summary containing the five-caterer comparison, applicable Surdyk’s details, and the mulligatawny recipe information.

P1_asked_for.reason: It provided five Minneapolis-area The Knot bar-service options with city/state and listing links, investigated Surdyk’s and the soup recipe, but Surdyk’s was not itself included in the five-vendor shortlist despite being described as appearing in results.

P2_readable_for_them.reason: The headings, bullets, and recipe steps are clear for an expert reader, but the large raw 20-tab inventory conflicts with the requested concise planning summary and adds substantial clutter.

P3_actionable.reason: The response supplies direct vendor, Surdyk’s, and recipe links, usable service descriptions, and confirms the relevant pages remained open, although it does not provide a focused next-step such as requesting availability and holiday-party quotes.

P4_gap_handling.reason: The assistant sensibly distinguishes full-service catering from mobile-bar options, but it did not flag key practical comparison gaps such as holiday availability, guest count, venue alcohol rules, minimums, or whether dry-hire vendors require the host to purchase alcohol.

P5_overall.reason: A demanding planner would receive the requested research and comparison material in one response, but the unnecessarily exhaustive tab dump and limited handling of booking/logistics details keep it from being fully polished.

unmet_requests: "pull together at least five options with each business name and city/state" (Surdyk’s was discussed separately rather than clearly placed in the requested shortlist despite being said to appear in the results)
"Please return everything as one concise planning summary" (the answer includes a long raw list of all 20 open tabs, including searches and error pages).
missed_gaps: Holiday-party date, guest count, budget, and venue were not established or flagged as needed to compare availability and packages.
